attempts.cause: The format_phone function incorrectly appends the remaining digits instead of truncating the last digit when formatting an 11-digit number.
attempts.candidate:
create or replace function format_phone(p_number in varchar2) return varchar2 is
  -- Formats an 11-digit mobile number as 0300-1234567; other input is returned unchanged.
  l_digits varchar2(40) := regexp_replace(p_number, '[^0-9]', '');
begin
  if length(l_digits) = 11 then
    -- The expected format is 4 digits - 7 digits (total 11 digits).
    -- The original code returned substr(l_digits, 4) which is 7 digits long, resulting in 4+1+7 = 12 characters if the input was 11 digits.
    -- If the input is 11 digits, we want the first 4 digits, a dash, and the remaining 7 digits.
    -- The test output suggests the expected format is 4 digits - 7 digits, totaling 11 digits including the dash, or 10 digits of numbers.
    -- Test 1: Input '03001234567' (11 digits). Expected: '0300-1234567' (4 + 1 + 7 = 12 characters).
    -- The bug report states "Mobile numbers on customer letters have one digit too many after the dash."
    -- If the input is 11 digits (e.g., 03001234567), and the expected output is '0300-1234567', then the second part must be 7 digits long.
    -- substr(l_digits, 4) returns 8 digits if l_digits is 11 digits long (11 - 4 + 1 = 8).
    -- We need to return substr(l_digits, 4, 7) to get exactly 7 digits.
    return substr(l_digits, 1, 4) || '-' || substr(l_digits, 5, 7);
  end if;
  return p_number;
end format_phone;
